title: Plane a marked wood face with a free bench plane
instruction: Take the bench plane from the moving carrier, plane the entire marked 90 by 40 mm section of the clamped board to remove all pencil marks, then return the plane to the carrier and release it.
context: A cabinetmaker uses a bench plane to make a smooth, even wood surface before fitting or finishing. The sole rides on the stock and sets the blade depth. The robot has to coordinate two independent grasps to keep the sole seated while feeding a continuous cut across the full marked width.
setup: Fixed YAM station; x forward, y left, z up, metres. Table top z=0.7475; arm bases (0,+/-0.305,0.750), grippers open, seed 0 and no jitter. A 5 kg 140x320x30 mm carriage starts at (0.300,0,0.7625), travels +/-30 mm in Y with an 8 s sinusoidal period and has +/-50 mm native guide limits. The rail/base solids and removable hardwood tool-rest deck are specified in assets/geometry.json. The free plane starts with sole-origin (0.300,0,0.7806), mass 1.8 kg, sole width/length 65/270 mm. Its compound geometry includes a 6 mm split sole, 4 mm cheeks, a 51x40x2 mm steel blade bedded at 45 degrees and projecting 0.1 mm below the sole, front hardwood knob at local Y=+100 mm and a rear hardwood tote at local Y=-100 mm. A No. 4 smoothing plane is the ordinary commercial form factor; the model is not a calibrated replica of a particular product. A fixed 60x400x25 mm softwood board is centred at (0.150,0,0.8100), top z=0.8225, in a steel vise. The 100x420x50 mm vise base is centred at (0.150,0,0.7725); two 10x400x20 mm jaws at X=0.115 and 0.185 have tops 5 mm below the wood face. Eighteen transverse 40x1.5 mm pencil stripes span the central 90 mm of the face. All component transforms, shapes, rail hardware, nominal material labels, contact patches and the passive cutting law are in assets/geometry.json and the dimensional reference.
scoring: At episode end, score is 0.75 times the union of successfully planed length divided by the 90 mm marked span. Repeated passes over the same place do not accumulate duplicate credit. Cutting credit requires consecutive loaded forward observations, the 51 mm blade covering the complete 40 mm stripe width, sole tilt at most 8 degrees, a forward-facing blade, blade-point height within 1.5 mm of the face, native normal load 20-80 N and an actually applied mean passive cutting load of at least 20 N. Forward travel exceeding 0.20 m/s is rejected as an observation jump. Loaded backward strokes, lifted passes and rubbing without the cutting load do not erase marks. Full score 1.0 requires at least 99% coverage, the entire plane inside the moving carrier with 5 mm XY border, its bottom within -1 to +4 mm of the carrier surface, linear speed relative to the carrier below 10 mm/s, angular speed below 0.5 rad/s, and both TCPs more than 100 mm from the plane's whole bounding box, continuously for 1 s. A tool falling more than 30 mm below the table scores 0; all other outcomes retain the applicable partial score.
run_limit: 800 control steps (40 simulated seconds at 20 Hz)
reset_notes: Restore all geometry transforms and the carriage phase. Replace or remark the same 90x40 mm face and zero coverage, material state and controller state. For a physical counterpart use a sharpened, properly adjusted ordinary bench plane and suitable clamped softwood, with the blade protected at rest. The simulated passive cutting law is nominal; physical wood removal and force response have not yet been measured.
fidelity: Native contacts and grasps carry the free tool. Rigid stock retains its mesh; a loaded-stroke rule removes visible marks. A passive 25 N blade load approximates cutting, bounded by contact and the native stopping impulse. Loads and material response are nominal, not calibrated. Wood fracture, chips and blade adjustment are omitted.
scores: Dream-1 beta run: 0.00; scripted native-contact demo: 1.00
